issues.body: `rewrite()` rejects only strings beginning with `refs/remotes/` or `remotes/`, before resolving the argument. Git commonly resolves `origin/ledger` to `refs/remotes/origin/ledger`, and `filter-branch` can update the resolved ref. Thus `rewrite --ref origin/ledger` bypasses the promised remote-tracking guard even though the README uses exactly that spelling for scans. The self-test covers only the already-expanded spelling, so it cannot detect this bypass. This violates the tool's stated one-local-branch safety boundary.
issues.fix_hint: Resolve the supplied revision to one unambiguous full ref before any scan or rewrite (for example with an exact symbolic-full-name check), require it to be under `refs/heads/`, and pass that resolved full name to every subsequent operation. Add red tests using a real `origin/ledger` shorthand and other non-head spellings, asserting that the ref and backup namespace remain unchanged.
issues.title: Remote-tracking shorthand bypasses the rewrite refusal

issues.body: `_commit_messages()` frames records with `\x01` and fields with `\x02` while claiming those bytes cannot occur in commit messages. Git commit messages prohibit NUL, but they can contain these control bytes. A message containing `\x01` can be split into an extra pseudo-record; content after it may land in the parsed `sha` field and never be examined for legacy subjects or literal handles. The scan can consequently return zero exposures despite a supplied handle remaining in reachable history, contradicting the fail-closed verification contract.
issues.fix_hint: Use Git's NUL-safe output framing (such as `-z` with NUL-delimited fields/records, or read commit objects individually from an independently enumerated SHA list) and validate every parsed SHA/field count. Add a real commit-object fixture containing `\x01` and `\x02`, with a known handle after each byte, and assert the literal verification remains non-zero without printing the handle.
issues.title: Commit-message separators are valid data, allowing a false-clean scan

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The purge and its self-test are substantial, but the rewrite boundary is not sound yet. The local-only ref check is performed on the caller's spelling rather than the ref Git resolves, so a normal remote-tracking shorthand bypasses it. Separately, the scan's commit-message framing relies on control bytes that Git does permit in commit messages; crafted history can therefore make the verifier omit message content and report a false clean result. Both defects affect the safety claims of the maintainer runbook and require changes.
